summary.headline: Capital SFB Q4 FY26 PAT rose 17% YoY to ₹40 crores, with NIM up to 4.06% and FY27 ROA guided to 1.35%–1.4%.
summary.overview: Gross advances reached ₹8,687 crores (+20.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ) and total deposits crossed ₹10,000 crores (+20% YoY). Q4 PPOP rose 28% YoY to ₹62 crores and cost of deposits eased to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ, with NIM at 4.06% versus 4.01% in Q3. Asset quality was broadly stable: GNPA 2.54%, NNPA 1.24%, with Q4 credit cost of 0.26% driven by higher provisioning (PCR 51.89%) rather than losses. Management guided to FY27 advances growth of 22%+, ROA of 1.35%–1.4%, and credit cost of 0.15%–0.25%.

segments.name: MSME / business banking
segments.commentary: Growth driver: +9% QoQ and +46% YoY in Q4. Management expects it to remain a growth leader in FY27.

segments.name: LAP (loan against property)
segments.commentary: +5% QoQ and +19% YoY; yield 12.33% in Q4 vs 12.56% in Q3. Named as a FY27 growth leader.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Book grew 7% QoQ but net NPA was static at 2.76% vs 2.75%. Growth to be slower than the overall book, limited to Punjab and Haryana.

segments.name: Mortgage / housing
segments.commentary: Housing yield 9.85% in Q4 vs 9.83% in Q3. Cited as a driver for growth in newer states.

segments.name: NBFC-MFI
segments.commentary: Outstanding net NPA ₹5.49 crores vs ₹6.08 crores a quarter earlier; total exposure about ₹39 crores. No fresh lending in Q4; an OTS was signed with one lender.

segments.name: Out-of-Punjab advances
segments.commentary: 24% of advances at March 2026 vs 21% a year earlier; growing more than twice the Punjab rate YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 secured advances growth of 22%+; advances above ₹16,000 crores by FY29.
Branches: target of 235 by end of FY27 (current year) and 300+ by FY29.
NIM expected to improve slightly in Q1 FY27 and more meaningfully in Q2; 53% of term deposits are high-priced and reprice in the next two quarters.
FY27 ROA target of 1.35%–1.4%, rising to 1.6%+ by FY29; ROE of 15%+ by FY29.
FY27 opex/average assets guided to 2.9%–3.0% (lower bias), with opex/average assets below 2.85% over the medium term.
FY27 credit cost guided to 0.15%–0.25% with negative bias; target of about 0.3% up to FY29.
Fee income/average assets guided to 0.85%–0.95% with upward bias; Banca to be expanded by one product in FY27 and one more later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 211 across 5 states and 2 union territories at March 2026; 77.3% are SURU branches.
Target of 235 branches by end of FY27 and 300+ by FY29; 50% of new branches to be opened outside Punjab and 40–45% in Punjab.
Management said cost of new branches in FY27 is mainly last-mile branch cost, as senior and head-office costs are already built in.
Business per branch (5+ year branches) is ₹106 crores in Punjab vs ₹73 crores outside Punjab; PPOP of 5+ year branches is 2.75%–3.25% vs 2.1% entity level.
demand_pricing: Disbursements were ₹919 crores in Q4 (+20% YoY) and ₹3,508 crores in FY26 (+23% YoY).
Average ticket size ₹18.3 lakh vs ₹17.8 lakh in Q3; about 98% of the book is secured and about 89% of the non-corporate book is backed by property or FDRs.

Yields: agriculture 12.54% (vs 12.62%), business 10.55% (vs 10.6%), corporate 10.77% (vs 10.8%); overall advance yield fell to about 10.8% from about 11.1%, partly due to a 25 bps rate cut and agri accounts moving to NPA with interest reversals.
Fee income was ₹25.8 crores in Q4 vs ₹26.1 crores in Q3 (0.9% of assets, vs 1.0% a year earlier); treasury income fell due to weaker market opportunities.
Cost of deposits 5.75% in Q4 vs 5.86% in Q3; average CD ratio 82.3%, period-end 86.7%; retail deposits above 90%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross NPA additions and provisioning: are provisions increasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹22 crore FY provision figure includes tax; PCR was raised to 51.89% from 50.45%, so provisioning was increased within the profit outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Agri NPA stickiness: will it fall back toward 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not target 2%; it expects agri NPA to stay range-bound with a lower bias. Recoveries concentrate in Q1 and Q3 cash-flow periods.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new ECL framework on credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial view is P&L neutral to positive, as current provisions are considered sufficient against the ECL requirement; detailed evaluation is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending / BC model and FLDG cover?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank runs a business correspondent lending model (not co-lending) with more than one partner, and the FLDG cover is 5% per regulation. Branches are to remain 90–95% of disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the NII margin expansion and CD ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposit repricing (53% repricing in Q1–Q2) and an improving CD ratio are the two NIM levers; management expects an opex/average assets ratio of 2.9%–3.0% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost and cost-to-income guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost for FY27 is 0.15%–0.25%. The Q4 credit cost of 0.26% was provisioning-driven, linked to NBFC-MFI slippage. Cost-to-income is expected to improve, with opex/average assets at 2.9%–3.0%.

risks_watch: Agri asset quality: net NPA at 2.76%, and monsoon or input-cost stress could affect the book, although management cites Punjab irrigation and collateral.
Pace of deposit repricing and whether NIM reaches the guided improvement in Q1–Q2 FY27.
Yield pressure: advance yields fell to about 10.8% amid rate cuts and NPA reversals; 8–10 bps of the decline is described as temporary.
Fee income and treasury income momentum; Banca and fee targets depend on new product approvals.
ECL transition impact, which management expects to be P&L neutral to positive but is still under evaluation.
Growth outside Punjab through business correspondent partners, which is early-stage and carries FLDG exposure.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed on growth and margin guidance, with specific numeric targets for FY27 and FY29. Management was defensive on agriculture NPA stickiness and the 0.26% credit cost, attributing both to provisioning and seasonality rather than losses.
key_quotes: So we are seeing some benefit, which will be pouring up from that repricing on their maturity.
So the current quarter credit cost is a provisioning driven, not a loss driven.
We are not doing agriculture in Rajasthan, UP, in Jammu, Himachal.

adds.what: Branch network target of 235 by end of FY27 (from 211 at March 2026) and 300+ by FY29

growth.why: Management guides FY27 secured advances growth of 22%+ and ROA of 1.35%–1.4%, backed by a branch build-out from 211 to a 235 target by end FY27 (about 11% more branches) and by disbursements up 23% in FY26; the brief gives no order-book or capex figures, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: Q1 FY27 slight, Q2 FY27 more meaningful
rows.why: NIM at 4.06% in Q4 vs 4.01% in Q3, with 53% of term deposits high-priced and repricing in the next two quarters; cost of deposits eased to 5.75% from 5.86%, and management guides a slight NIM improvement in Q1 and a more meaningful one in Q2. Yield pressure (advance yield ~10.8% from ~11.1%) is a partial offset.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY27 (235 branches by end FY27), 300+ by FY29
rows.why: Branches at 211 at March 2026 with a firm target of 235 by end FY27, about 11% more branches, and the build-out is already under way with 50% of new branches outside Punjab.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides secured advances growth of 22%+ for FY27 after advances grew 20.9% YoY to ₹8,687 crores and disbursements rose 23% in FY26 to ₹3,508 crores.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 PAT rose 17% YoY and ROA reached 1.33% in Q4 vs 1.16% in Q3, but FY27 ROA guide of 1.35%–1.4% is only modestly above the 1.23% FY26 level, so an upgrade depends on sustaining the Q4 run rate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Agri net NPA is 2.76% and stuck, NBFC-MFI slippage drove the 0.26% Q4 credit cost against a FY27 guide of 0.15%–0.25%, and yields fell to ~10.8% from ~11.1%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans to expand Banca by one product in FY27 and one more later, and fee income guidance of 0.85%–0.95% of average assets depends on new product approvals.

rows.label: Term deposit repricing lifts NIM
rows.why: 53% of term deposits are high-priced and reprice in the next two quarters, with cost of deposits already down to 5.75% from 5.86% QoQ.

rows.label: Opex/average assets held at 2.9%-3.0%
rows.why: Cost-to-income fell to 58.2% in Q4 from 61% for FY26, and the 5+ year branches run PPOP of 2.75%-3.25% vs 2.1% at entity level, with new branches mainly last-mile cost.

rows.label: Out-of-Punjab growth via BC partners
rows.why: Out-of-Punjab advances are 24% of the book vs 21% a year earlier, and 50% of new branches are to open outside Punjab, though the BC model is early-stage with 5% FLDG exposure.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 22%+ FY27 growth, NIM repricing, and branch build-out to 235, and defensive on agri NPA stickiness and the 0.26% Q4 credit cost, which it attributed to provisioning. Analysts pressed on asset quality and provisioning.
